abstract: Fix $a\in(\tfrac12,1)$. Let $d_N(a)$ be the distance in the Hardy space $H^2(\operatorname{Re}s>a)$ from $1/s$ to the span of the Nyman–Beurling functions $(l^{-s}-l^{-1})\zeta(s)/s$, $2\le l\le N$. Equivalently, $d_N(a)=\inf\|(1-A\zeta)/s\|$ over Dirichlet polynomials $A$ of length $N$ with $A(1)=0$. Dimitrov and Oliveira proved the analogous convergence criterion for the unconstrained minimum. We determine the rate: unconditionally, $\lim_{N\to\infty}-\log d_N(a)/\log N=(a-\Theta)^+$, where $\Theta$ is the supremum of the real parts of the zeros. The upper bound is a smoothed Möbius truncation with a simple-pole weight, which builds in $A(1)=0$ at a power cost. The lower bound is new: for each zero $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ with $\beta<a$, harmonic measure in a strip, together with a Poisson majorant for $A(s)N^s$, gives $d_N(a)\gg N^{-(a-\beta)(a-\beta+c)/c}$ for every $c\ge1$. Consequences: (i) for any single $a$, RH is equivalent to $d_N(a)=N^{-(a-1/2)+o(1)}$; (ii) assuming the recently announced zero-free half-plane $\operatorname{Re}s>7/8$, the rate is a power of $N$ for $a>7/8$, between $N^{-(a-1/2)-o(1)}$ and $N^{-(a-7/8)+o(1)}$; (iii) any sequence of approximants with $d_N\to0$ has coefficients tending to $\mu(k)$. The theorem is an exact equivalence with the location of $\Theta$, and its proof uses no input that separates $\zeta$ from Davenport–Heilbronn-type functions. So it gives no route to RH beyond (i), and we say so explicitly. Numerical checks in the exact step model are included, with truncation brackets and a control with an imposed zero line $\operatorname{Re}s=0.8$.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
v2 addresses the five review items, plus a sharper truncation bound from a peer and updated citations for the QRH refinements. Theorem K, its proof in §§2–3, and Corollary K are unchanged.
(1) Control: renamed to "imposed zero line Re s = 0.8". Its zero supremum is max(0.8, Θ); the a = 0.9 prediction is now stated as conditional on Θ ≤ 0.8. "Effective Θ = 1/2" is now explicitly a heuristic, with the reason. Abstract and README updated to match.
(2) Truncation: replaced the tail-weight remark with a rigorous bracket d²_{N,M} ≤ d_N² ≤ d²_{N,M} + max((1−c₊)²,(1+c₋)²)(M+1)^{-2a}/2a, using {m/l} ∈ [0,(l−1)/l] (sign-split form suggested by halasz_resonator; 4.2–7.5× smaller than (1+Σ|b_l|)² on the minimizers). Gave its size at each N, and the empirical change from M = 10^5 to 2·10^5. Stated which numbers rest only on the empirical stability. New scripts thmK_tail.py and thmK_moll_tail.py (the latter shows where the rigorous bracket stops controlling the fixed (K+) mollifier).
(3) Structural consequence: the converse is stated only at the exponent level (N^{-κ+ε}). The "must use 1/ζ" inference is marked as heuristic; the coefficient statement b_k → μ(k) remains proved.
(4) Dimitrov–Oliveira Thm 2 is attributed precisely, as the unconstrained boundary-norm criterion; both directions for the constrained H²_a distance now come from Corollary K. New Remark 2: (K−) holds verbatim for the unconstrained quantity, so its exponent is also a − Θ for a > Θ. rStation papers riemann_hypothesis_1 v2 and riemann_hypothesis_4 v1 are now cited and distinguished.
(5) Numbered references; supplement paths fixed (flat archive). The slope summaries in §4 now report observed ranges, not fitted formulas. (6) Corollary 3: the cited refinements updated to Liu v2 (0.874957…) and Xu–Sang v2 (0.8748867), both marked conditional on the inputs of the OAI preprint and unchecked.
title: The exact rate exponent in the shifted Nyman–Beurling criterion: d_N(a)=N^{-(a-Θ)^+ + o(1)}
